candidate.title: HydEn-seq
candidate.scope: The single HydEn-seq row of the assigned Illumina DNA poster: hydrolytic end sequencing of genomic ribonucleotides, clarified by Clausen et al. (2015), PMID 25622295. HydEn-Seq / Hydrolytic DNA End Sequencing in the paper names the same target method. Inventory: Genome; Ribonucleotides / R on antiparallel DNA; Alkaline hydrolysis (KOH); a 5′HO fragment with 2′,3′-cyclic phosphate; Phosphorylation (T4 PNK 3-phosphatase minus); 5′P-O fragment; Ligate oligo with 5′-amino-terminated C6 spacer; Add sequencing primers, PCR and sequence; Map locations on the genome. Arrows support one linear route, with no sample split, pooling or alternative branch. Rapture, Digenome-seq and Ribose-seq are adjacent independent rows, and the chemical legend at the right is contextual. They do not expand this card’s method scope. Broad library preparation remains broad; this is not a complete laboratory protocol or a claim about unshown adaptations.

states.label: Genomic DNA with embedded ribonucleotides
features: The diagram shows antiparallel DNA strands with embedded R residues, not an RNA transcript analyte.

The paper implementation uses budding-yeast genomic DNA; RER deficiency and replicase variants provide biological contexts for interpreting polymerase-specific patterns, rather than extra transformations in this schematic.

states.label: Strand-specific map of inferred genomic ribonucleotide positions
features: The diagram’s final black genome line is marked R at mapped positions.
In the paper, aligned 5′-end positions are shifted one base upstream on their respective strands to identify the hydrolyzed ribonucleotide; reference sequence supplies its base identity.
End counts and strand patterns can report ribonucleotide incorporation and, in supported yeast genetic contexts, replicase usage. A mapped 5′ end alone does not prove which polymerase made the DNA.

This is an end-mapping readout. The paper specifically considers mitochondrial contributions from pre-existing strand nicks or alkali-sensitive abasic sites; a mapped end alone is therefore not proof of a ribonucleotide.

operations.label: Alkaline hydrolysis (KOH)
operations.description: Hydrolyze ribonucleotide-containing genomic DNA to single-stranded fragments, converting alkali-sensitive ribonucleotide sites into mappable DNA boundaries. The drawing specifies 5′ hydroxyl and opposite 2′,3′-cyclic-phosphate ends.
operations.mechanism: Alkaline cleavage at embedded ribonucleotides; the paper attributes alkali sensitivity to the ribose 2′ oxygen.
operations.information_effect: Transfers positional information from an embedded ribonucleotide into the adjacent downstream DNA fragment’s 5′ boundary.

operations.label: Phosphorylation (T4 PNK 3-phosphatase minus)
operations.description: Convert the hydrolyzed fragment’s 5′ hydroxyl into a 5′ phosphate for subsequent oligo ligation. The opposite cyclic-phosphate icon remains unchanged in the depicted state.
operations.mechanism: 5′ phosphorylation by the explicitly named 3′-phosphatase-minus T4 polynucleotide kinase; kinase is a reagent acting on DNA, not a transferred sample branch.
operations.information_effect: Prepares the captured genomic 5′ boundary for tagging without changing the genomic sequence it denotes.

operations.label: Ligate oligo with 5′-amino-terminated C6 spacer

operations.description: Align the DNA-fragment reads to a reference genome to assign positions and strands. The paper resolves the interface between a mapped end and the target residue: shift a mapped 5′ end one base upstream to locate its hydrolyzed ribonucleotide.

operations.information_effect: Produces the depicted R-location map. Replicase-specific interpretation requires the biological comparisons described in the paper; an end position alone is not a polymerase identifier. Other sources of DNA ends limit target specificity.

method_scopes.rationale: All five operations lie on the row explicitly labeled HydEn-seq and form its uninterrupted route. Clausen et al. explicitly names HydEn-Seq and describes the same KOH cleavage, 3′-phosphatase-minus kinase, ARC140 ligation, library sequencing and end mapping. The poster’s replicase-specific purpose is supported by the paper’s RER-deficient yeast and replicase-variant comparisons; those sample genotypes are not extra depicted operations or universal input requirements. No neighboring workflow is an alternative target of this schematic.
